subject: Post-demo: Performance/SLO checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mejia <carlos@fintechco.com>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintechco.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: Performance/SLO checklist & next steps

Hi Carlos / Jane —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through the demo. Really appreciate the clarity on the primary performance goals — wanted to summarize the SLO targets you gave and propose next steps so we can scope a short proof-of-performance.

Recap of the requirements you mentioned on the call:
- Latency: P95 end-to-end (client->Redwood->client) <= 200 ms for streaming single-token latencies; goal P95 <= 150 ms if possible for 256-token responses.
- Throughput / concurrency: sustain 100 concurrent active streams per region (initial target), spike to 200 concurrent for short bursts; ~180 RPS peak observed on demo workload.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming with flush every token (low-latency partial outputs) and keepalive support for long-running responses (up to 30s).
- Payload: average prompt size ~1.2k tokens, average response size ~300 tokens; some outliers up to 2k tokens.
- Availability/ops: target 99.9% SLA, canary rollout required prior to Prod, and region preference us-east1.

Proposed immediate next steps (MAP):
1) Redwood provides a short SLO checklist & test plan (attached) and a recommended load test profile by EOD Monday (Dec 1).
2) You provide sample payloads and a representative traffic pattern (CSV or JSON) and confirm region(s) for testing.
3) We run a staged perf test (canary -> small scale -> ramp to peak) and share detailed breakdown (P50/P95/P99 for token latency, throughput, CPU/GPU utilization) within 72 hours of receiving payloads.
4) Decide success criteria: if P95 <= 200 ms at 100 concurrent streams with <= 25% cost uplift vs baseline, move to pilot.

I've looped in Rishi (SE) to own the test plan. Attaching a lightweight SLO checklist and the demo recording for reference.

Attachments: redwood_slo_checklist.xlsx; demo-recording.mp4

Happy to jump on a 30m call early next week to run through the test plan live. What times work for you?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Carlos Mejia <carlos@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance/SLO checklist & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the clear MAP. Quick clarifications from our side based on additional internal questions:

- The 200 ms P95 target is for perceived token latency (i.e., time between token generation and client receiving that token) for streamed responses. For full-response times we expect P95 <= 2s for the 300-token average.
- Concurrency: 100 concurrent streams is our steady-state target; we need to tolerate 200 concurrent for short bursts (1-5 minutes).
- Regional constraint: primary is us-east1; we will want failover to us-west1.
- Security/compliance: we will need a short note on data handling during load tests (no production PII should be used in sample payloads).

Action items from FintechCo:
- We will extract a week of representative traffic patterns and sanitize payloads by Friday (Dec 3).
- We can provide sample payloads and a small test harness (JMeter scripts) if Redwood prefers.

If you can send the SLO checklist + recommended load profile, we will prioritize getting the sanitized data and pick a slot for the canary test next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the test plan.

Best,
Carlos
VP, Platform Engineering — FintechCo
carlos@fintechco.com

Carlos / Jane —

Appreciate the fast reply. Attaching the SLO checklist and a concise load-profile recommendation. High-level notes below; the attached checklist includes exact test commands and dashboards we will share.

Quick technical notes / assumptions we encoded in the plan:
- Test harness will exercise token streaming (server-sent events) and full-response paths.
- Ramp plan: canary (10 streams) -> small-scale (50 streams) -> steady-state (100 streams for 15 minutes) -> burst (200 streams for 2 minutes) -> cooldown.
- Metrics reported: P50/P95/P99 token latency, end-to-end full response time, GPU util, batch size distribution, KV-cache hit rate, request/response token counts.
- Failure criteria: P95 token latency > 200 ms sustained for >5 minutes or error rate >1% at steady-state.

Proposed MAP with rough dates:
- Dec 1 (EOD): Redwood delivers final test plan + test AMI and monitoring dashboard link (we will share an invitation).
- Dec 3: FintechCo provides sanitized payloads and any synthetic traffic multipliers.
- Dec 6-7: Run staged perf tests and share detailed report by Dec 8.

Links: demo recording and hubspot deal: https://drive.redwood/demo-recording.mp4 | https://hubspot.com/deal/12345

Attachments: redwood_slo_checklist.xlsx

Thanks Marissa — looping in a couple of quick technical clarifications so we scope the load correctly.

Rishi: a few notes for Carlos / Jane:
- Please include a small sample of "worst-case" long responses (1.5k-2k tokens) in the payload bundle so we can validate KV-cache behavior and memory pressure.
- Provide expected respawn/connect patterns (e.g., how often clients reconnect mid-stream) — this affects connection churn and is important for keepalive tuning.
- For the streaming test, we will measure token latency as "time from token ready in runtime -> socket send" plus network RTT; please confirm whether FintechCo will run the client-side collection in us-east1 so we can minimize cross-region noise.

Aditya (cc): comments?

Aditya Rao: ACK — we have a short infra playbook to run the staged test on dedicated capacity; I will start prepping the canary image and the dashboards.

Carlos / Jane — if you can drop the sanitized payloads to the shared Drive link by EOD Dec 3 we will schedule the canary for Dec 6 morning (US PST) and send calendar invites.

Thanks —
